topic: API performance testing and resource allocation
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on stress testing the API's performance, particularly concerning frequency and resource limits. Initial concerns about memory exhaustion during high concurrent requests were addressed by increasing allocated resources (CPU/memory) for both staging and production environments.

Testing involved simulating a large volume of concurrent requests (up to 1000 requests with 50 parallel connections). The results indicated that the system is now stable under load, with memory usage remaining low even during stress tests. It was noted that the API handles high volumes of long-running requests without crashing.

Technical discussions covered resource allocation best practices (e.g., container limits vs. node capacity) and troubleshooting monitoring issues (Grafana/Prometheus).

Separately, a plan to load unique traffic data separately onto the traffic dashboard was discussed.
decisions: The API resources for staging and production were confirmed to be configured similarly with one instance each.
Increased resource allocation helped stabilize the system under high concurrent load.
A feature to load unique traffic data separately onto the traffic dashboard is planned.
action_items: Someone needs to investigate why monitoring metrics are not collecting correctly in Grafana/Prometheus.
Follow up on potential issues with incoming requests logged via Rollbar for frequency tracking.
